children.objective: Explore OpenMP data-parallel execution over disjoint output indices, using the caller's threads value as an upper bound and avoiding parallel-region overhead for a one-thread call. Keep the supplied per-element arithmetic and CND unchanged. Write every output on every call, preserve correctness for all valid sizes and inputs, and compare timings at both official thread budgets; record any case where parallel overhead outweighs the benefit.
children.subject: Thread-budgeted parallel loop

children.objective: Explore SIMD execution across the full per-element Black-Scholes calculation, including vector arithmetic for the supplied CND polynomial and vectorized or otherwise SIMD-compatible log, sqrt, and exp operations. Retain the supplied CND coefficients/formula as the algorithmic reference so this tests a vectorized-kernel approach distinct from T3's scalar lower-work CND approach. Do not change compiler flags or assume an ISA beyond what the build supports. For arbitrary valid n, use alignment-safe accesses and handle tails; the 64-byte input base does not guarantee aligned array sections, and output alignment is unspecified. Any approximations must satisfy the fixed tolerance over the valid input domain; use a safe fallback where needed. Respect the caller's thread budget, overwrite all outputs, and validate and measure both official sizes and thread budgets on varied and constant inputs.
children.subject: SIMD for full Black-Scholes kernel

children.objective: Explore reducing the work in the scalar CND evaluator alone, for example through Horner evaluation or a lower-cost piecewise/rational approximation with robust symmetry and tail behavior. Keep the outer Black-Scholes calculation and loop organization unchanged to isolate this opportunity. Preserve the required tolerance for all valid inputs, including varied and constant inputs, and measure at both sizes and thread budgets.
children.subject: Lower-cost CND evaluation

model_interpretation.claim: Les variantes de seuil déjà mesurées sont correctes, mais leurs moyennes agrégées visibles dépassent celle de f164 et ne donnent pas les temps par motif et par taille. Je garde donc le seuil de 8192 et le calcul SIMD inchangés, et teste une distribution statique par blocs de 128 itérations SIMD (1024 éléments) plutôt qu'une seule grande portion contiguë par thread. Si le coût des chemins de repli scalaire varie entre blocs, cette granularité pourrait améliorer l'équilibrage à 4 threads, surtout sur entrées variables; si l'accès moins contigu ou la granularité accrue domine, les temps peuvent régresser. Le contrôleur doit mesurer chaque cas face à f164; arrêter en cas d'échec de correction ou sans gain répétable à 4 threads sans régression sur les cas constants et à 1 thread.
